mainTopic: The end of the חבת הקודש question, the משנה on signs of life for a slaughtered מסוכנת, and the גמרא's search for a source that a מסוכנת is permitted.
overview: The amud opens by closing a question from the previous daf: does חבת הקודש only disqualify a holy item itself, or does it also let us count a ראשון and שני from it? The question ends in תיקו, unresolved. A new משנה then deals with slaughtering a מסוכנת, an animal in danger of dying, which needs a sign that it was alive at the שחיטה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי אליעזר, רבי שמעון and חכמים disagree about which sign is enough: leg movement, spurting blood, or a tail wag. The משנה adds that stretching out a foreleg without pulling it back does not count, and that a healthy animal needs no sign at all. The גמרא then asks how we know a מסוכנת can be permitted at all, since 'זאת החיה אשר תאכלו' could mean 'eat only an animal that can live.' It tries a proof from the איסור of נבלה, and then one from the איסור of טרפה, but each is pushed off by suggesting the categories overlap. Finally it turns to the פסוק about the חלב of a נבלה and a טרפה, which teaches that one איסור can take effect on top of another. The proof built on that פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does regard for holiness also create further levels of impurity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes stating a question: does חבת הקודש only disqualify the item itself, or does it also let that item pass impurity on to a ראשון and שני?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the answer? When regard for holiness works, maybe it only disqualifies the item itself, but does not let us count first-degree and second-degree impurity from it. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question that began on the previous daf. The question asks how far the power of חבת הקודש reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally food must get wet before it can become impure. חבת הקודש is a rule that holy items can become impure even without being wet. The question is whether this rule gives the item only a weak status (it is disqualified itself), or a full impure status that passes on further levels (ראשון, then שני).

keyTerms.meaning: Regard for holiness. Holy items are treated as able to become impure even without the normal step of getting wet.
Disqualifying the item itself.
First-degree and second-degree levels of impurity.
Or perhaps there is no difference.

phrases.english: What is the answer?
phrases.notes: This finishes a question that started on the previous daf.

phrases.english: When regard for holiness is effective,
is it only to disqualify the item itself,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לְמִימְנֵא בֵּיהּ רִאשׁוֹן וְשֵׁנִי לָא,
phrases.english: but not to count first and second degree from it,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a question from the previous daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חבת הקודש gives an item full impurity status that passes on levels of impurity, or only disqualifies the item itself.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question about חבת הקודש is left without an answer: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says it has no answer to the question, so it is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו is not a ruling in either direction. It simply means no source settles the question.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question stays unresolved.

steps.whatToRemember: Whether חבת הקודש can create a ראשון and שני stays an open question (תיקו).

phrases.english: It shall stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question in step 1 without an answer.

steps.title: A dying animal needs a sign of life: two opinions
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: when slaughtering a מסוכנת, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs both the foreleg and the hind leg to convulse, while רבי אליעזר says spurting blood is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone slaughters an animal in danger of dying. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is valid only if it convulses with its foreleg and its hind leg. רבי אליעזר says it is enough if the blood spurted out.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses what sign proves that a dying animal was still alive when it was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מסוכנת may already have died before the knife cut, so we need proof of life after the שחיטה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל asks for a strong sign: movement in both legs. רבי אליעזר accepts a forceful spurt of blood as proof.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal in danger of dying soon.
That it convulses or jerks.
Foreleg and hind leg.
It spurted, meaning the blood shot out forcefully.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who slaughters an animal in danger of dying,
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Only if it convulses with the foreleg and the hind leg.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
It is enough if it spurted.
phrases.notes: The thing that spurts is the blood from the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: both foreleg and hind leg must convulse. רבי אליעזר: spurting blood is enough.

steps.title: Blood on the walls proves it spurted
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון gives a case: someone slaughters at night and finds the walls full of blood the next morning. The animal is valid, following רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: Someone slaughtered at night, got up early the next day, and found the walls full of blood. The animal is valid, because the blood spurted. This follows the rule of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון backs up רבי אליעזר with a practical case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when nobody saw the animal at the moment of שחיטה, blood splashed on the walls shows that it spurted. By רבי אליעזר's rule, that alone proves the animal was alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Walls.
Valid, kosher.
In accordance with the rule or approach of.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
One who slaughters at night,
and the next day he got up early
and found walls full of blood —
it is valid, since it spurted,
and this follows the rule of Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אליעזר's opinion to a practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood found on the walls proves it spurted, so the animal is valid according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: The Rabbis: one leg or a tail wag is enough
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say the animal is valid if it convulses with either the foreleg or the hind leg, or if it wags its tail.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis say: It is valid only if it convulses with the foreleg or the hind leg, or if it wags its tail.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים give a third opinion. They require movement, but less than רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said 'foreleg and hind leg'. חכמים say 'foreleg or hind leg', so one is enough, and they add a tail wag. Unlike רבי אליעזר, they still require movement, not just spurting blood.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, the majority opinion.
That it wags its tail.

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the small word difference: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says 'בַּיָּד וּבָרֶגֶל' (both legs), but חכמים say 'אוֹ בַיָּד אוֹ בָרֶגֶל' (either one).

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁתְּפַרְכֵּס אוֹ בַיָּד אוֹ בָרֶגֶל,
phrases.english: Only if it convulses either with the foreleg or with the hind leg,
or if it wags its tail.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁתְּפַרְכֵּס אוֹ בַיָּד אוֹ בָרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third opinion, between רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Convulsing with one leg, or wagging the tail, is enough.

steps.title: Small and large animals; stretching out the foreleg does not count
steps.stepSummary: These rules apply to both small and large animals. A small animal that stretches out its foreleg and does not pull it back is invalid, because that is just the soul leaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies to both a small animal and a large animal. A small animal that stretched out its foreleg and did not bring it back is invalid, because that is only the soul leaving the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that the rules apply to every size of animal. It also names one movement that does not count as a sign of life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every movement proves life. Stretching a leg out without pulling it back is what happens naturally as an animal dies. So it shows nothing about being alive at the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: A small domesticated animal, such as a sheep or goat.
A large domesticated animal, such as a cow.
Invalid.
The soul leaving the body, the dying process.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה וְאֶחָד בְּהֵמָה גַּסָּה,
phrases.english: Both a small animal and a large animal.
A small animal that stretched out its foreleg,
and did not bring it back — it is invalid,
since that is only the soul leaving the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה וְאֶחָד בְּהֵמָה גַּסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines which movements count as a sign of life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stretching out the foreleg without pulling it back is not a sign of life, so the animal is invalid.

steps.title: These signs are needed only for an animal known to be dying
steps.stepSummary: The signs are needed only when the animal is presumed to be a מסוכנת. A healthy animal is valid even with no sign at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this said? When the animal was presumed to be in danger of dying. But if it was presumed healthy, then even if it shows none of these signs, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits all the rules above to an animal already known to be dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is the animal's חזקה, its known status before the שחיטה. A healthy animal is presumed to be alive when slaughtered, so no proof is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? It introduces a limit on the rule.
Presumed to have the status of.
Healthy.
Signs or indicators, here the signs of life.

steps.whatToRemember: Signs of life are needed only for a מסוכנת. A healthy animal is valid without any sign.
steps.whyThisMatters: The animal's known status before the שחיטה decides whether any proof of life is needed at all.

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
Where it was presumed to be in danger of dying,
but if it was presumed to be healthy,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אֵין בָּהּ אֶחָד מִכׇּל הַסִּימָנִים הַלָּלוּ –
phrases.english: even if it has not one of all these signs —
it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? שֶׁהָיְתָה בְּחֶזְקַת מְסוּכֶּנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits all the earlier rules to a מסוכנת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Signs of life are required only for an animal presumed to be dying. A healthy animal is valid without them.

steps.title: Why is a dying animal allowed at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a מסוכנת becomes permitted through שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know that an animal in danger of dying is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for a source for the משנה's basic assumption that a מסוכנת can be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only discussed which signs are needed. It took for granted that a dying animal can be permitted at all. The גמרא wants proof of that starting point.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? Asks for a source.
That it is permitted.

phrases.english: Gemara:
An animal in danger of dying — from where do we know it is permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the משנה's assumption.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a מסוכנת is permitted through שחיטה.

steps.title: Why would we think it is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with its own question: what reason is there to think a מסוכנת is forbidden in the first place?
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where would it enter your mind that it is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the question, asking why anyone would think a source is needed. This sets up the next step, which gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slaughtered animal is normally permitted, so a source is only needed if there is a reason to forbid it. This forces the questioner to name that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter our mind, meaning would we think so?
That it is forbidden.

phrases.english: And from where would it enter our mind that it is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A counter-question to the question in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reason there could be to think a מסוכנת is forbidden.

steps.title: The verse could mean: only eat an animal that can live
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why one might forbid a מסוכנת: the פסוק 'זאת החיה אשר תאכלו' could mean you may eat only an animal able to live, and a מסוכנת cannot live.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written: 'These are the living beings that you may eat.' Eat what can live, and do not eat what cannot live. And an animal in danger of dying cannot live, can it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for thinking a מסוכנת might be forbidden, using a reading of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חיה in the פסוק could be read as 'a living creature that can survive.' On that reading, only an animal able to live is permitted, and a מסוכנת seems to be left out. This is why the original question in step 8 needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written, introducing a פסוק.
Here it means a living being, one able to live.
It is not able to live.

steps.confusionAlert: In this פסוק, חיה does not mean a 'wild animal' as it often does. The reading here takes it as 'a living creature that can survive.'

phrases.english: As it is written:
"These are the living beings that you may eat,"
one that can live, eat;
and one that cannot live, do not eat.
And an animal in danger of dying cannot live, can it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by giving the reason one might forbid a מסוכנת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'זאת החיה אשר תאכלו' could be read as permitting only an animal that can live, which would leave out a מסוכנת.

steps.title: A first proof from the איסור of נבלה
steps.stepSummary: Since the תורה bothered to forbid a נבלה, a dead animal, a מסוכנת must be permitted. If even a living מסוכנת were forbidden, there would be no need to forbid it after it dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה said 'do not eat a נבלה.' That shows a מסוכנת is permitted. If a מסוכנת were forbidden while still alive, why would the תורה need to tell us it is forbidden after it dies?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings its first proof that a מסוכנת is permitted when slaughtered. The proof comes from the פסוק that forbids a נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every animal that dies on its own was a מסוכנת just before it died. If being a מסוכנת were already enough to make it forbidden, the later איסור of נבלה would add nothing. So the תורה forbidding נבלה shows that the earlier stage, מסוכנת, is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה
By implication; we learn it from what is implied
Permitted / forbidden
'Now if X is so, is Y even needed?' This shows that a statement would be extra

phrases.english: From the fact that the Merciful One said 'you shall not eat a נבלה,'
we learn by implication that a מסוכנת is permitted,
for if it entered your mind that a מסוכנת is forbidden,
now, if it is forbidden while still alive,
is it necessary to say it is forbidden after death?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא נְבֵלָה לֹא תֹּאכֵל, מִכְּלָל דִּמְסוּכֶּנֶת שַׁרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry from step 10 that a מסוכנת might be forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק נבלה לא תאכל would be extra if a מסוכנת were forbidden

steps.title: Maybe נבלה and מסוכנת are the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: maybe the word נבלה itself includes a מסוכנת, so the פסוק is not extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe 'נבלה' and 'מסוכנת' are the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the proof. Maybe the פסוק of נבלה is itself the איסור of a מסוכנת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if נבלה means a dead animal, which is a later stage than מסוכנת. If the word נבלה also covers a dying animal, then the פסוק is not extra. It would be the very source that forbids a מסוכנת.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps; it opens a challenge
That is the same as
'X is the same as Y'; the two are one category

phrases.english: But perhaps a נבלה is the same
as a מסוכנת?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in step 11 that נבלה means only a dead animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If נבלה includes a מסוכנת, the פסוק is not extra and proves nothing

steps.title: The תורה calls an animal נבלה only after it dies
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק about טומאה shows that the word נבלה is used only after death, so a living מסוכנת is not called a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot be. The פסוק says: 'If an animal that you may eat dies, whoever touches its נבלה...' So only after death does the תורה call it a נבלה. While it is alive, it is not called a נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof from step 11. It shows from a פסוק that the word נבלה means a dead animal only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first says 'if it dies' and only then calls it 'its נבלה.' That shows a נבלה is defined by death. So נבלה cannot include a living מסוכנת, and the proof of step 11 stands for now.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that idea is rejected
Its carcass
While alive
After death

phrases.english: That cannot enter your mind,
for it is written: 'And if any animal dies'
'that is yours to eat,'
'one who touches its carcass...'

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר מִיתָה הוּא דְּקַרְיַיהּ רַחֲמָנָא נְבֵלָה,
phrases.english: it is after death that the Merciful One calls it a נבלה;
while alive, it is not called a נבלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining a term from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נבלה might include a living מסוכנת
steps.terutzMaskana: נבלה means only a dead animal

steps.title: Maybe there are two איסורים: an עשה while alive and a לאו after death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא knocks down the proof. Maybe a מסוכנת is forbidden while alive by an עשה, and the פסוק of נבלה adds a לאו after death. Then that פסוק is not extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps, really, I can tell you that a נבלה and a מסוכנת are the same in their law. While alive it is forbidden by an עשה, and after death it is forbidden by a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from נבלה. The פסוק of נבלה could be adding a stronger kind of איסור, not a brand-new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said the פסוק of נבלה would be extra. But if a living מסוכנת is forbidden only by an עשה (from 'זאת החיה אשר תאכלו' in step 10), the פסוק of נבלה still teaches something new: after death there is also a לאו. So the proof falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually; it holds on to the original idea
A positive commandment; here, an איסור learned from a positive פסוק
A negative commandment, 'do not'

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a נבלה stops being a dead animal. It means both carry the same איסור of eating, but with different levels: an עשה while alive and a לאו after death.

phrases.english: But perhaps, really, I could tell you:
a נבלה is the same as a מסוכנת,
while alive, it is forbidden with a positive commandment;
phrases.notes: This is the עשה from 'זאת החיה אשר תאכלו' in step 10: eat only an animal that can live.

phrases.english: after death, it is forbidden with a negative commandment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even after step 13, it brings down the proof of step 11
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק of נבלה is not extra, since it may add a לאו on top of an עשה

steps.title: A second proof from the איסור of טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The תורה forbids a טרפה, an injured animal. If a מסוכנת, which is whole, were forbidden, then a טרפה, which is damaged, would surely be forbidden. So the איסור of טרפה shows that a מסוכנת is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תורה said 'do not eat a טרפה.' That shows a מסוכנת is permitted. If a מסוכנת were forbidden, then since even a מסוכנת that is missing nothing is forbidden, would we need a פסוק to forbid a טרפה?
steps.whatsHappening: After the first proof failed, the גמרא brings a new proof from the איסור of טרפה. The structure is the same as the first proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה is worse than a מסוכנת because its body is damaged. If even a whole מסוכנת were forbidden, the איסור of טרפה would be obvious and extra. The escape of step 14 does not fit here, because both animals are alive, so there is no 'before death and after death' split. Step 16 tries a different way to push back.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; it drops the old proof and starts a new one
An animal with a fatal injury or defect
Lacking, damaged in its body

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from נבלה fails because it could be adding a לאו after death. The proof from טרפה argues that if a whole מסוכנת were forbidden, the תורה would not need to forbid a damaged טרפה. Step 16 challenges this proof, and step 18 finally knocks it down.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the second attempt to find the source for the משנה's assumption that a slaughtered מסוכנת can be kosher. Like the first attempt, it will be pushed off (steps 16–18).

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, מִדְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא טְרֵפָה לֹא תֹּאכַל –
phrases.english: Rather, from the fact that the Merciful One said 'you shall not eat a טרפה,'
we learn by implication that a מסוכנת is permitted,
for if it entered your mind that a מסוכנת is forbidden,
now, if a מסוכנת that is not lacking anything is forbidden,
phrases.notes: The מסוכנת is weak but its body is whole. A טרפה is injured or missing something.

phrases.english: is it necessary to forbid a טרפה?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִדְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא טְרֵפָה לֹא תֹּאכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was rejected in step 14
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק טרפה לא תאכל would be extra if a whole מסוכנת were forbidden

steps.title: Maybe the word for an injured animal also covers an animal in danger
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from טרפה. Maybe a מסוכנת is included in the word טרפה, so it is forbidden by both an עשה and a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps a טרפה and a מסוכנת are the same thing, and a person would break both a positive command and a prohibition by eating it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 15. Maybe the תורה's word טרפה already includes a מסוכנת, so the איסור of טרפה proves nothing about a מסוכנת being permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 assumed that טרפה means only a damaged animal, separate from a whole מסוכנת. The גמרא now suggests that both fall under the one word טרפה. On that view, eating either one breaks both an עשה and a לא תעשה, so there is no proof that a מסוכנת is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces a way to push back on a proof)
An animal with a fatal injury or defect
An animal in danger of dying but not physically damaged
A positive command and a prohibition

phrases.english: But perhaps a tereifa is the same
as an animal in danger of dying,
and one would violate both a positive command and a prohibition for it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from טרפה brought in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the איסור of טרפה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes that טרפה does not include a מסוכנת. Maybe it does, with an עשה and a לאו on both.

steps.title: Then why forbid a dead animal at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 16. If a living מסוכנת were already forbidden by a לאו and an עשה, the תורה would not need to forbid it after death as a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need the נבלה that the תורה wrote? If while the animal is alive there is already a לאו and an עשה on it, do I need to be told it is forbidden after it dies?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 16. If a מסוכנת were forbidden even while alive, the פסוק of נבלה would be pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a living מסוכנת already carries both a לאו and an עשה, it is obviously forbidden once it dies. So the פסוק of נבלה must be teaching something, and that only makes sense if a living מסוכנת is permitted. This brings back the reasoning of step 11 in a stronger form.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a problem with the idea just said)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Why do I need it? (the wording seems extra)
While still alive
Is it needed? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: If so,
why do I need the carcass that the Merciful One wrote?
If while it is alive
one already stands over it with a prohibition and a positive command,
is it necessary to say so after death?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, נְבֵלָה דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion of step 16 by asking what the פסוק of נבלה would add.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a living מסוכנת is forbidden under the word טרפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it were forbidden while alive, forbidding it after death would be obvious, so the פסוק of נבלה would have no purpose.

steps.title: Maybe all three words mean the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question aside. Maybe נבלה, טרפה and מסוכנת are all one category. Then the פסוק of נבלה adds a second לאו, and the animal carries two לאוין and an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps נבלה, טרפה and מסוכנת are all the same thing, and a person would break two prohibitions and a positive command!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 17. The פסוק of נבלה is not pointless, because it may simply add another לאו to the same animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 assumed that נבלה means only a dead animal. Here the גמרא suggests that the word נבלה also covers a טרפה and a living מסוכנת. Then the פסוק is not extra: it adds a second לאו on top of the לאו of טרפה and the עשה. So this line of proof falls.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Two prohibitions
This is the same as

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with step 13, which showed that נבלה is used only after death. Here the גמרא is just raising a possibility to stop the proof. It is not deciding what the word נבלה really means.

phrases.english: But perhaps a carcass is the same
as a tereifa and as an animal in danger of dying,
and one would violate two prohibitions and a positive command for it!
phrases.notes: The two לאוין are the ones of נבלה and טרפה. The עשה is the same one mentioned in step 16.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא הַיְינוּ נְבֵלָה, הַיְינוּ טְרֵפָה, הַיְינוּ מְסוּכֶּנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 and ends this attempt at a proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the פסוק of נבלה is extra
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק could add a second לאו if נבלה also covers טרפה and מסוכנת.

steps.title: A new proof from the verse about forbidden fat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier proofs and brings a new source, the פסוק about the חלב of a נבלה and the חלב of a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learn it from here: "The fat of a נבלה and the fat of a טרפה may be used for any work, but you shall not eat it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new proof that a מסוכנת is permitted, beginning with a פסוק about חלב. This step only quotes the פסוק and sets up the argument that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proofs could all be pushed off by saying the words overlap. So the גמרא turns to a different פסוק, one that names נבלה and טרפה together with חלב. The proof itself is built on this פסוק in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here (drops a failed proof and brings a new one)
Forbidden fat of an animal
Work or use (here, any use other than eating)

phrases.english: Rather, it is learned from here:
"And the fat of a carcass and the fat of a tereifa
may be used for any purpose,
but you shall not eat it,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since the proofs from נבלה and טרפה were rejected, a new source is brought.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 7:24, about the חלב of a נבלה and a טרפה

steps.title: The verse makes one prohibition land on top of another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a known teaching. The פסוק teaches that the איסור of נבלה and the איסור of טרפה take effect even on חלב, which is already forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Master said: For what law did the תורה say this? So that the איסור of נבלה will come and take effect on the איסור of חלב, and the איסור of טרפה will come and take effect on the איסור of חלב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an earlier teaching that explains what this פסוק comes to teach. This is still setup; the actual proof about מסוכנת will be built on it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once something is forbidden, a second איסור does not land on it. This פסוק teaches that the איסורים of נבלה and טרפה do take effect on חלב, so a person who eats such fat breaks both איסורים. The proof that a מסוכנת is permitted is built on this teaching on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (what does this פסוק teach in practice)
Let it come and take effect
One prohibition taking effect on top of another

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is the base of the new proof. The proof itself, built on the rule that one איסור lands on another, comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: And the Master said:
For what law did the Torah say this?
phrases.notes: Using fat for work is not the new point here. He is asking what the mention of נבלה and טרפה adds.

phrases.english: Let the prohibition of a carcass come
and take effect on the prohibition of fat;
let the prohibition of a tereifa come
and take effect on the prohibition of fat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר מָר: לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא אָמְרָה הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what the פסוק quoted in step 19 teaches, as the base for the new proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The איסורים of נבלה and טרפה take effect on the already existing איסור of חלב.
